public_rationale: Primary evaluations document remaining reasoning failures, but also substantial gains in novel-task adaptation. Neither finding establishes whether the field had a reliable general solution to any entire prerequisite. The field-wide negative is broader than the retrieved evidence, and its undefined standard materially affects the result.
limitations: A narrow successful algorithm would not refute the contextual claim about general capabilities.
A benchmark failure would not rule out other methods.
The ARC result concerns the tested December preview, not later released versions of o3.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In the quarter century since 2001, none of the listed AGI prerequisites (generalization, abstract reasoning, tracking individuals, understanding structure) has received a principled solution.

statement.excerpt: What that means is that a quarter century has passed without a principled solution to even one of those problems.
statement.document_title: Ezra Klein’s new take on AGI – and why I think it’s probably wrong

from_speaker: to even one of those problems
our_interpretation: The four problems are generalization to new instances, abstract reasoning, tracking individuals and properties without hallucination, and understanding complex syntax and semantics.
The plain contextual reading of a principled solution is a reliable general method for at least one capability, not a narrow task-specific algorithm or benchmark improvement.
Treat quarter century as approximate. The stated history runs from the book’s writing in 2000 through March 5, 2025.
Evidence of failures in selected models cannot by itself establish that the entire field lacks a solution.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently broad research record establishes that all four capabilities still lack reliable general solutions by the post date.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A reproducible, established method provides a reliable general solution to at least one of the four capabilities by the post date.

evidence.explanation: The tested models show fragility under controlled changes to mathematical questions. This supports concern about reliable reasoning in those models, but does not establish a field-wide absence of solutions to all four capabilities.

evidence.locator: Section So is it AGI?; opening results paragraphs
evidence.explanation: ARC Prize reports 75.7% and 87.5% on its semi-private evaluation for two compute settings of the tested o3 preview, describing substantial progress in novel-task adaptation. It also documents remaining easy-task failures, so the result neither proves a general solution nor supports an absence of progress.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An explicit capability-level standard and a comprehensive assessment of proposed methods through March 5, 2025, or a reproducible general solution meeting that standard for one listed capability.
